# The map of packages/world

One line per file, in what the file says of itself. The kinds of folder are in [README.md](../README.md).

## `docs/`

- [`account.md`](../docs/account.md): Serve the account's operations
- [`api.md`](../docs/api.md): How a world's api is hosted and reaches its parts
- [`cluster.md`](../docs/cluster.md): How the cluster works
- [`commands.md`](../docs/commands.md): Make, list and destroy a world by hand
- [`containers.md`](../docs/containers.md): How a refused container start is tried again
- [`images.md`](../docs/images.md): Pin or publish an image
- [`lessons.md`](../docs/lessons.md): What was learned building the world
- [`proofs.md`](../docs/proofs.md): Run a proof
- [`renew.md`](../docs/renew.md): Renew a world
- [`reset.md`](../docs/reset.md): Reset a world in place
- [`sites.md`](../docs/sites.md): How a world's sites are made on the bench

## `src/account/`

- [`lists.ts`](../src/account/lists.ts): world.list, world.snapshot.list and world.snapshot.delete, as the platform serves them: what an operator has on the platform (packages/blueprint, src/world/inventory.ts).
- [`operators.ts`](../src/account/operators.ts): Who may call the platform: its two operators, each by the name the platform gives them and the token that signs them in (decisions.md, 16 and 37).
- [`refusals.ts`](../src/account/refusals.ts): How the platform's handlers keep their declared refusals and nothing else: any other failure of what they call (a deploy, a database, the shared state) is a fault, which the caller sees as a defect (decisions.md, 10).
- [`serve.ts`](../src/account/serve.ts): `world platform serve`: the platform group served on this machine's loopback until the process is stopped, for a caller on the same machine (decisions.md, 51).
- [`server.ts`](../src/account/server.ts): The platform's door: the blueprint's platform group (world.create, world.show, world.snapshot.save, world.snapshot.restore, and an operator's inventory: world.list, world.snapshot.list and world.snapshot.delete), served over HTTP with Effect's Rpc server at `PLATFORM_PATH` by whatever process runs it where the Cloudflare and Neon keys are (decisions.md, 51): the runner, in-process, or `world platform serve`.
- [`snapshots.ts`](../src/account/snapshots.ts): world.snapshot.save and world.snapshot.restore, as the platform serves them (decisions.md, 17 to 19, 46 and 51).
- [`store.ts`](../src/account/store.ts): What the platform keeps of its own, in the schema `platform` of the registry's branch (the platform stage's), beside the registry of world names: the spans of every platform call, which world each successful call acted on (its events are in that world's record), and every snapshot a world has saved.
- [`view.ts`](../src/account/view.ts): What the platform answers of a world, and the events it writes into a world's record.
- [`worlds.ts`](../src/account/worlds.ts): world.create and world.show, as the platform serves them (decisions.md, 13 to 15, 20 and 25).

## `src/cli/`

- [`commands.ts`](../src/cli/commands.ts): The world command line: one small set of commands over the package's Effect API.
- [`main.ts`](../src/cli/main.ts): The entry: the only file that touches the process.
- [`renew.ts`](../src/cli/renew.ts): `renew <name> --lifetime "7 days"`: a world that is meant to last (a shared world) given a later expiry and deployed again with the code that runs now (src/things/world/renew.ts).
- [`report.ts`](../src/cli/report.ts): What every command shares: where its result goes, and how a lifetime is written.

## `src/common/`

- [`describe.ts`](../src/common/describe.ts): One line that says why something failed: its tag and its message, never a stack trace and never a secret.
- [`failures.ts`](../src/common/failures.ts): The world package's own failures, declared here once.
- [`record.ts`](../src/common/record.ts): What a run leaves behind once its world is gone, and what a proof saw.
- [`stopwatch.ts`](../src/common/stopwatch.ts): A step of a world's life: run under its declared timeout, with its duration written down whether it ended well, failed or timed out (roadmap rule 6).

## `src/`

- [`index.ts`](../src/index.ts): The package's one import entry: everything another package may import.

## `src/parts/api/`

- [`Api.ts`](../src/parts/api/Api.ts): The one place that decides what runs in a world's Core slot: the real Core (packages/core), deployed with the world and handed the world's own facts (CoreDeployment), never its own stage's:  its database      the world's branch, through the world's Hyperdrive configuration (WorldDatabase) its world door    the world's token on the hub (src/things/cluster/client.ts) and the owner operator's token (`operator-token`) its chain         a service binding to the hub's door, whose `/<token>/rpc` is the chain; Core answers only the blueprint's reads at CHAIN_PATH its tap           on in a world of a test grade (`private`, `shared`): every OTLP body Core exports is also kept in the world's `telemetry.otlp`; never in a `real` world its sites         the site door of the world's bench and the world's site token there, and the credential of the API user the door makes on each of the world's sites (`site-key`, `site-secret`); none when the world has no bench  Every token is an Alchemy.Random of the world's stage, kept in the shared state, bound to the Worker as a secret and read back from the state (parts.ts), never an output.
- [`health.ts`](../src/parts/api/health.ts): Core's door, as the world needs it: the one path that says Core is up, Core's own (packages/core, src/probe.ts).
- [`host.ts`](../src/parts/api/host.ts): Core run off Cloudflare, beside the machine that makes the world: a rehearsal's seam (packages/runner, `--core=local`).
- [`steady.ts`](../src/parts/api/steady.ts): A world runs once its Core answers steadily.

## `src/parts/bundler/`

- [`Alto.ts`](../src/parts/bundler/Alto.ts): The bundler's container: Pimlico's alto 0.0.21, built from images/alto.
- [`Bundler.ts`](../src/parts/bundler/Bundler.ts): One world's bundler.
- [`Keys.ts`](../src/parts/bundler/Keys.ts): What the world's bundler, its test paymaster and whoever sends a UserOperation agree on.
- [`client.ts`](../src/parts/bundler/client.ts): The world's bundler, reached from outside: one ERC-4337 JSON-RPC call through the world's door, and what the bundler says about its own starts and stops.
- [`setup.ts`](../src/parts/bundler/setup.ts): The world's bundler, brought up when the world is created (the `bundler` step): its two accounts are funded from the chain's faucet, the test paymaster is put on the chain and given its deposit at the EntryPoint, and alto is started and waited for.

## `src/parts/chain/`

- [`Anvil.ts`](../src/parts/chain/Anvil.ts): The chain's container: anvil, built from images/anvil/Dockerfile with the repository's seeded state baked in.
- [`Chain.ts`](../src/parts/chain/Chain.ts): One world's chain, on the hub (src/things/cluster): one object per world, by the world's stage.
- [`ChainState.ts`](../src/parts/chain/ChainState.ts): Where a stopped chain's state is kept: one object per chain.
- [`abi.ts`](../src/parts/chain/abi.ts): The little of the Solidity ABI the platform sends: a call's data from its selector and its arguments, static (address, uint, bool, bytes32) and dynamic (bytes, string).
- [`admission.ts`](../src/parts/chain/admission.ts): The world a chain belongs to on the hub: kept by the world's chain object when the world is registered, and checked on every call to the world (src/parts/gateway/Gateway.ts).
- [`calls.ts`](../src/parts/chain/calls.ts): How the chain's Durable Object talks to its anvil: one JSON-RPC body forwarded as it is, or one of anvil's methods called for the chain's own needs, over the container's port.
- [`contracts.ts`](../src/parts/chain/contracts.ts): What every world's chain holds before anything is sent to it: the seeded chain's last block and the addresses of the contracts a world's claims read.
- [`controls.ts`](../src/parts/chain/controls.ts): The world's controls at its hub's door that an in-place reset and a snapshot's save need (src/things/world/reset.ts, src/account/snapshots.ts): the chain rewound to a snapshot, and the index stopped and resumed.
- [`faucet.ts`](../src/parts/chain/faucet.ts): The world's test USDC and its faucet.
- [`objects.ts`](../src/parts/chain/objects.ts): Removing everything of one world from the hub's bucket: its chain's saved state, its snapshots' states, then its entry in the hub's ledger (src/things/cluster/registration.ts).
- [`record.ts`](../src/parts/chain/record.ts): What the chain's Durable Object remembers about its own starts and stops, kept in its storage and given out by `GET /chain/status`.

## `src/parts/containers/`

- [`patience.ts`](../src/parts/containers/patience.ts): Starting one of a world's containers from its Durable Object, patiently.
- [`record.ts`](../src/parts/containers/record.ts): What the world's Durable Objects keep about their containers' starts and stops: when, as ISO text, and the latest few of each.
- [`stop.ts`](../src/parts/containers/stop.ts): Stopping a container so its process can shut down cleanly: SIGTERM, then wait for it to exit, and only a process that outlives the grace is killed.

## `src/parts/database/`

- [`Database.ts`](../src/parts/database/Database.ts): A world's one database: its own copy-on-write branch of the Neon project the platform stage owns (made through Neon's API, src/parts/database/neon.ts), and the Hyperdrive configuration through which the world's Core reaches it.
- [`branches.ts`](../src/parts/database/branches.ts): A snapshot's database: a branch of the world's own branch, made through Neon's API with no compute of its own, so it costs only the storage it does not share with its parent.
- [`neon.ts`](../src/parts/database/neon.ts): A world's branch through Neon's API, where Alchemy's own Neon provider is slow: it looks at a branch's operations every 5 s, so a branch whose compute is ready in 1 to 2 s takes 6 to 9 s in a deploy (spikes/world-speed; this package's `records/hub` spans).
- [`sql.ts`](../src/parts/database/sql.ts): The way in to a world's database from outside Cloudflare: Neon's HTTPS SQL endpoint.

## `src/parts/gateway/`

- [`Gateway.ts`](../src/parts/gateway/Gateway.ts): The hub's door (src/things/cluster): the one address of every world's chain, index and bundler on the hub.

## `src/parts/indexer/`

- [`Indexer.ts`](../src/parts/indexer/Indexer.ts): One world's index.
- [`Ponder.ts`](../src/parts/indexer/Ponder.ts): The index's container on the hub: the real Ponder app of packages/indexer, built from ponder/Dockerfile with the repository's packages/ folder as the context.
- [`starts.ts`](../src/parts/indexer/starts.ts): What the index's own record says about its starts, in one line, for the run record of a create whose index step failed: the index's Durable Object, and its record with every try, is destroyed with the world right after.
- [`timeline.ts`](../src/parts/indexer/timeline.ts): Where an index start's time goes, from Ponder's own metrics (`GET /metrics`, Prometheus text), read once when the index is first seen ready: when the Node process began, when Ponder began and ended its historical sync, and how long it spent in the database and on the chain.

## `src/proofs/`

- [`cases.ts`](../src/proofs/cases.ts): The package's proofs, by name.

## `src/proofs/cases/`

- [`bundler.ts`](../src/proofs/cases/bundler.ts): Proof: a world made by the one command holds a bundler and a test paymaster, and one UserOperation signed by a test key and sponsored by the paymaster lands on the world's chain as one transaction.
- [`clock.ts`](../src/proofs/cases/clock.ts): Proof: a world restored from a snapshot keeps the world's one clock.
- [`commands.ts`](../src/proofs/cases/commands.ts): Proof: one command creates a private world and another destroys it, run exactly as the README documents them, each as its own process.
- [`endings.ts`](../src/proofs/cases/endings.ts): Proofs about how a run ends: a use that fails, times out or is interrupted ends with its world destroyed, and a failed world that is kept on purpose is left stopped and is still deleted when its keep ends.
- [`fresh.ts`](../src/proofs/cases/fresh.ts): Proof: a world made from nothing answers on every part (chain, index, Core and database), a second world made from it starts with its rows and its chain, and destroying both leaves the accounts as they were.
- [`hub.ts`](../src/proofs/cases/hub.ts): Proof (roadmap step 1.15): on the fleet hub, `world.create` makes a world whose chain, index and bundler answer and whose Core answers, with its migrations and its cast, in under 20 s, and `world destroy` removes it in a few seconds, its Durable Objects' state and its saved chain states included.
- [`patience.ts`](../src/proofs/cases/patience.ts): Proof: a world's containers are started patiently (src/parts/containers/patience.ts).
- [`reset.ts`](../src/proofs/cases/reset.ts): Proof (roadmap step 1.16): a world reset in place to its snapshot.
- [`shared.ts`](../src/proofs/cases/shared.ts): Proofs about what worlds share: two creates of one name at once, the limits on private worlds, and the sweeper over an expired world, a live one and one with no recorded expiry.
- [`site.ts`](../src/proofs/cases/site.ts): The proof of a world's company site on a shared bench (roadmap step 1.4), on the bench `WORLD_BENCH` names:  1.
- [`snapshot.ts`](../src/proofs/cases/snapshot.ts): Proof: the platform's four operations, called as its handlers are called (src/account), make a world with its cast and its start block, save it whole and restore it into a second world that holds exactly what was saved, while the first goes on alone; every refusal the operations declare for these cases is answered and makes nothing; and destroying both leaves nothing of either, snapshot branches included.

## `src/proofs/support/`

- [`conclude.ts`](../src/proofs/support/conclude.ts): What every proof shares: its checks and its record, the inventory it takes before and after, and the world command line run as its own process, as a person or a schedule runs it.
- [`payments.ts`](../src/proofs/support/payments.ts): What the proofs do inside a world: pay from a funded address through the world's RPC address, and wait for the index to write what happened to the world's database.
- [`userop.ts`](../src/proofs/support/userop.ts): One real ERC-4337 v0.7 UserOperation in a world, for the bundler proof.

## `src/stack/`

- [`cloud.ts`](../src/stack/cloud.ts): What the two accounts hold, read straight from Cloudflare's and Neon's own APIs, not from Alchemy's state: the listing that shows a destroy left nothing behind, and the image repositories that `alchemy destroy` does leave.
- [`engine.ts`](../src/stack/engine.ts): The only file that drives Alchemy: deploying and destroying a stage of the stack, and reading the shared state store.
- [`images.ts`](../src/stack/images.ts): The three images every world runs, and how a deploy names each one.
- [`names.ts`](../src/stack/names.ts): The names every part of the package agrees on.
- [`settings.ts`](../src/stack/settings.ts): What the caller decides about a world, handed to the stack as a service around a deploy.

## `src/things/cluster/`

- [`client.ts`](../src/things/cluster/client.ts): The fleet hub from outside: bringing a hub up and down (`./run.sh hub up|down|show`), and what a world's life asks of it: registering the world (its owner, its expiry and its token's secret), forgetting it, and the hub's ledger.
- [`idle.ts`](../src/things/cluster/idle.ts): What a hub runs right now, from Cloudflare's own listing of its container applications: how many instances of each are active (running, and billed) against those merely placed in advance.
- [`registration.ts`](../src/things/cluster/registration.ts): A world on the hub: what the hub keeps of it, and where.
- [`stage.ts`](../src/things/cluster/stage.ts): The fleet hub's stack (roadmap step 1.15).
- [`values.ts`](../src/things/cluster/values.ts): The names every part of the hub agrees on.

## `src/things/registry/`

- [`reserve.ts`](../src/things/registry/reserve.ts): The registry of world names: one row per world, in a table on the platform's own Neon branch.
- [`stage.ts`](../src/things/registry/stage.ts): The platform stage: what every world shares.

## `src/things/site-template/`

- [`keep.ts`](../src/things/site-template/keep.ts): A world's company sites kept as a bench template (roadmap 1.17 and 1.18; docs/roadmap.md, "Bench templates never change"; src/things/site/reset.ts and src/things/site-template/sweep.ts): a runner that keeps one world for its run makes each starting world in it once, saves it as a snapshot and keeps its sites as a bench template, so a later reset whose point lost its sites claims them ready instead of building them.
- [`sweep.ts`](../src/things/site-template/sweep.ts): Bench templates: what a template is named, what code made it, and the sweep that removes old ones (docs/roadmap.md, decision "Bench templates never change", 14 November 2026; packages/platform, door/templates.py).

## `src/things/site/`

- [`bench.ts`](../src/things/site/bench.ts): A world's company sites on a shared bench (roadmap step 1.4; the decision "Site creation on a shared bench").
- [`client.ts`](../src/things/site/client.ts): One call to a bench's site door (packages/platform, door/door.py), with a world's site token: answered at once (`doorCall`), or run by the door as a job and polled (`doorJob`).
- [`reset.ts`](../src/things/site/reset.ts): A world's company sites across an in-place reset (roadmap 1.16 to 1.18): saved to a point of the bench with the world's snapshot, and put back in place to it when the world is reset.
- [`snapshot.ts`](../src/things/site/snapshot.ts): A world's company sites in its snapshots (blueprint decisions.md, 17): saving them with the snapshot, and making them again in a world restored from it.

## `src/things/world/`

- [`bring-up.ts`](../src/things/world/bring-up.ts): Bringing one world up on its fleet hub, step by step: the claim, its registration on the hub, then the chain's lane and the database's lane side by side.
- [`cast.ts`](../src/things/world/cast.ts): A new world's cast and its clock's start on its chain (decisions.md, 20, 25 and 42).
- [`client.ts`](../src/things/world/client.ts): The parts of a deployed world, reached from outside: its door (chain and index), its Core, and its record in the shared state.
- [`create.ts`](../src/things/world/create.ts): Creates one world outside a run and leaves it up for its owner.
- [`destroy.ts`](../src/things/world/destroy.ts): Destroys one world by name, from the shared state alone.
- [`expiry.ts`](../src/things/world/expiry.ts): The pure decisions about a world's life: when it expires, and what its record in the shared state says about it at a given moment.
- [`handle.ts`](../src/things/world/handle.ts): A deployed world's handle: what its stage's outputs record and the secrets worked out from them, each secret kept for the life of the process under what it was worked out from (src/things/world/kept.ts).
- [`kept.ts`](../src/things/world/kept.ts): What a world's handle is built from, kept for the life of the process: a world.show cost 0.7 to 1.35 s a call, about 300 calls a run, because every call asked Neon for the connection string, read the hub's admin token and the world's operator token from the shared state, and opened the hub (design-notes/speed.md, change 3).
- [`list.ts`](../src/things/world/list.ts): Every world the shared state holds, as a listing shows it.
- [`names.ts`](../src/things/world/names.ts): What a caller may call a world and its owner.
- [`renew.ts`](../src/things/world/renew.ts): Renewing a world that is meant to last, such as a shared world (roadmap step 2.3): the SAME world, its name, branch, data, chain, sites and snapshots kept, given a later expiry and deployed again with the code that runs now.
- [`reset.ts`](../src/things/world/reset.ts): Resetting a world in place to one of its snapshots (roadmap 1.16): the SAME world, its name, door, Core and token unchanged, rewound to what the snapshot saved, with one clock.
- [`stage.ts`](../src/things/world/stage.ts): The stack.
- [`store.ts`](../src/things/world/store.ts): A world's facts in its own database (packages/core/migrations/0003_world.sql): its chain's contracts, its clock (in the shape Core's site operations keep it), its cast and its companies, and its record (app.events), whose latest `world_created` says its grade and its parent.
- [`sweep.ts`](../src/things/world/sweep.ts): The sweeper: deletes every world whose recorded expiry has passed, and leaves the rest (roadmap rule 2).
- [`take-down.ts`](../src/things/world/take-down.ts): Bringing one world up, taking it down and parking it, step by step.
- [`use.ts`](../src/things/world/use.ts): The life of a world as one unit: create it, use it, write its record outside it, destroy it.
- [`values.ts`](../src/things/world/values.ts): What a caller says about the world it wants, what it is handed back, and the declared settings every world lives by: the limits on private worlds and the timeout of every step.
